report.summary: Audited 52 clients over 20 rounds (model: FedAvg logistic regression) using all 20 epsilon. Screened all clients with client_updates (c2, c12), client_performance (c3, c11), drift_by_round (c4), feature_summary (c5), subgroup_outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup and Income (c6-c8), plus narrower drift checks on VI, GU, NC, WY (c9) and attribution_churn (c10). No client carries a consistent, noise-adjusted flag on any fault signature, and none of the leads survived confirmation. Update-level screens (poisoning, free-rider, explanation instability) show no norm-ratio or cosine anomalies; the lowest-cosine clients (GU, MS, NM, NC) are small or have normal norms, and GU's cosine was not stable across two calls. Performance screens show no sustained label-noise or prevalence-shift pattern; AUC values moved a lot between calls at this noise level (e.g. NV 0.87 to 0.98), so single-call AUC outliers are not reliable. The only flags (CT AUC z=+3.1, GU CITL z=-3.1) are below the threshold and point the wrong way for label noise. Drift leads (VI, GU, NC, WY) are isolated spikes that jump between rounds rather than persistent shifts, consistent with small-sample noise. Feature-tail outliers (GU, VI, NC, TN, DE, WY, NV) are from small clients and show no consistent sentinel pattern. Subgroup outliers (CT, MI, ME, TX, VA, NH, AK, NC) are mostly tiny-subgroup noise and do not show the under-diagnosis pattern (low O/E with high FNR). Conclusion: no client is confidently faulty; the federation appears clean.
